title: Bundle Size Optimization
definition: The architectural reality that Tailwind naturally scales to a flat curve in production; no matter how large the application gets, the CSS file stops growing.
simpleExplanation: In traditional CSS, every new feature adds 100 new lines of CSS. A 50-page app might have a 500kb CSS file. In Tailwind, once you've used `flex`, `p-4`, and `text-center` once, they are in the bundle. Building 50 more pages uses those same exact classes. The CSS file literally stops growing around 15kb.
realWorldExample: Netflix completely rewriting their UI. They found that traditional CSS grew infinitely. Moving to utility-first CSS resulted in an extremely small, strictly capped CSS payload.

basic: Which results in a smaller production CSS file: Traditional semantic CSS or Tailwind CSS?
intermediate: If you use `bg-red-500` in 1,000 different React components, how many times does `bg-red-500` appear in the final production CSS file?

answers.question: Smaller CSS file?
answers.answer: Tailwind CSS. Because it reuses a strict set of utilities, its file size is exponentially smaller than traditional CSS at scale.

answers.question: How many times in CSS?
answers.answer: Exactly ONCE. The HTML references it 1,000 times, but the browser only downloads the CSS definition one single time.
